stories.headline: Meituan open-sources LongCat-2.0, a 1.6T coding model trained entirely on Chinese chips

key_facts.fact: Meituan officially released and open-sourced LongCat-2.0 on Tuesday, June 30, under a permissive MIT license, distributed via GitHub, Hugging Face and its native platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan officially unveiled LongCat-2.0 on GitHub, Hugging Face and its native platform... brings a native 1-million-token context window to the public domain under a highly permissive, enterprise grade, commercially viable MIT license.

key_facts.fact: LongCat-2.0 is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters, dynamically activating roughly 48 billion per token, with a native 1-million-token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan has released what it claims is the country's first trillion-parameter artificial intelligence model trained entirely on home-grown hardware... LongCat-2.0, a new large language model boasting 1.6 trillion parameters and a context window of 1 million tokens.

key_facts.fact: It is the first trillion-parameter model fully pre-trained and run on a cluster of more than 50,000 domestically made Chinese ASICs, without Nvidia GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: LongCat-2.0 is the industry's first AI model with more than a trillion parameters to be fully trained and run on a cluster of 50,000 domestically made chips, Meituan said. It did not disclose which Chinese chipmaker's products were used.

key_facts.fact: Meituan says LongCat-2.0's performance is comparable to Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, released in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Meituan says the performance of its new large language model, LongCat-2.0, is comparable to Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, which was released in February.

key_facts.fact: LongCat-2.0 was the previously anonymous stealth model 'Owl Alpha' that topped global developer charts on OpenRouter for the past two months.
key_facts.excerpt: unmasking the model as the computational engine behind 'Owl Alpha,' the anonymous stealth model that has spent the last two months commanding global developer charts on OpenRouter.

key_facts.excerpt: Through the agreement, state agencies may access Anthropic's AI productivity assistant, Claude, at a 50% discounted price... The agreement also provides the same discounted offer for California's local governments, including cities and counties.

key_facts.fact: The deal includes free workforce training plus technical assistance and workflow input from Anthropic developers, and makes Claude the first AI productivity tool available to all state agencies via the Department of Technology's new SITeS portal.

Claude is the first AI productivity tool that will be available to all State agencies though the California Department of Technology's new Statewide Information Technology Shared Services (SITeS) portal.

key_facts.fact: California already uses Claude in several departments: CalOES and CDT for cyber defense (scanning and patching state code), the DMV to cut customer wait times, and the Department of Healthcare Services, the largest Medicaid agency in the country, for internal workflows.

key_facts.fact: Departments will pay to use Claude individually with no statewide budget allocation, and no department had started using it under the new contract as of the announcement.

stories.headline: Amazon weighs OpenAI and own Nova models as Anthropic shifts to costlier token pricing

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on June 29 that Amazon is exploring OpenAI and its own Nova models after a renegotiated Anthropic contract shifts billing to per-token pricing next year, which could sharply raise Amazon's AI costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon is looking for cheaper alternatives to Anthropic's Claude models after a renegotiated contract will shift to token-based pricing that could substantially increase the company's AI costs, according to The Information... Amazon is already exploring options including OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's reliance on Claude runs deep, powering its Kiro coding agent, its Quick workplace assistant and Alexa for Shopping.
key_facts.excerpt: Its coding agent Kiro, workplace assistant Quick, and consumer-facing Alexa for Shopping all rely on Anthropic's models, according to The Information. A shift to token-based billing would make that dependence far more expensive.

key_facts.fact: Some Amazon engineers are already distilling Anthropic models into smaller, cheaper internal versions; Amazon holds certain rights to do so, similar to Apple's arrangement with Google Gemini.
key_facts.excerpt: some Amazon engineers are already distilling Anthropic models to build smaller, cheaper versions for internal use... Amazon has certain rights to use Anthropic's models for this purpose, according to a person familiar with the matter, similar to Apple's arrangement with Google Gemini.

key_facts.fact: Amazon disputed the report, saying the expanded partnership won't raise costs, while Anthropic said its per-token price keeps falling and called Amazon one of its most important partners.
key_facts.excerpt: An Amazon spokesperson pushed back, saying the changes from the expanded partnership won't raise costs. Anthropic points to lower prices relative to the performance its models deliver.

key_facts.fact: The strain follows large cross-investments: Amazon committed up to $50 billion to OpenAI this year and has invested a potential $33 billion in Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: Earlier this year Amazon committed $50 billion to OpenAI... That deal followed Amazon's initial $4 billion investment in Anthropic, which has since grown to a potential $33 billion.

stories.headline: Taiwan raids Super Micro offices, widening Nvidia AI-chip smuggling probe

key_facts.fact: Taiwanese government agencies raided Super Micro Computer's Taiwan offices and several local affiliates on Monday, June 29, deepening an investigation into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China using the company's servers.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer and several of its local affiliates, deepening an investigation into the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips into China using the company's servers.

key_facts.fact: Twelve sites were raided Monday, including the homes of six people and the offices of Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and Taiwan-listed firms Albatron Technology and Chief Telecom.
key_facts.excerpt: Twelve sites were raided on Monday as part of the probe... They included the homes of six people and offices of the companies they worked for - Nasdaq-listed Super Micro Computer and Taiwan-listed firms Albatron Technology and Chief Telecom.

key_facts.fact: Nine people are now under investigation, up from three previously, the head prosecutor of the Keelung Prosecutors Office told AFP.
key_facts.excerpt: Nine people are now under investigation, up from three previously, Huang Sheng, head prosecutor in the Keelung Prosecutors Office, told AFP.

key_facts.fact: Suspects are accused of forging documents to ship roughly 50 Super Micro servers containing advanced Nvidia chips to China, Macau and Hong Kong; some were cleared by Taiwan customs and sent to China via Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: They are accused of forging documents so they could ship roughly 50 servers made by Super Micro Computer to China. Some of the servers were cleared by Taiwan customs and sent to China via Japan.

key_facts.fact: Super Micro shares fell more than 9% on the news; the raids mark Taiwan's first formal crackdown on AI chip diversion after years of US pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro shares fell more than nine percent on the news... The raid extends Taiwan's first formal crackdown on AI chip diversion, which began in May.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan does not currently treat AI chip exports to China as a crime; the only legal recourse is to charge suspected smugglers with violations of other existing local laws.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan does not currently treat AI chip exports to China as a crime... the only legal recourse through the island's courts is to charge suspected smugglers with violations of other, existing local laws.

stories.headline: Supreme Court lets Trump fire FTC commissioner, overturning 90-year agency-independence precedent

key_facts.fact: In a 6-3 ruling on June 29, the Supreme Court upheld Trump's firing of FTC Commissioner Rebecca Slaughter, overturning the 1935 Humphrey's Executor precedent that shielded independent-agency officials from at-will removal.
key_facts.excerpt: the Supreme Court has voted to allow President Donald Trump to remove a Democratic member of the Federal Trade Commission, Rebecca Slaughter, for policy reasons, rolling back 90 years of legal precedent.

key_facts.fact: Chief Justice John Roberts wrote that Congress's 'for cause' removal protections violate the separation of powers, stating 'The President may remove his subordinates at will.'
key_facts.excerpt: Writing the majority opinion, Chief Justice Roberts said Congress' "for cause" removal protections, meant to shield independent agencies from political influence, violate the separation of powers.

key_facts.fact: The decision affects more than two dozen independent bipartisan agencies including the SEC, FCC and FEC, effectively ending their insulation from presidential control; Justice Gorsuch wrote 'Independent agencies are not so independent after all.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Independent agencies are not so independent after all," conservative Justice Neil Gorsuch wrote in a concurring opinion to the majority decision.

key_facts.fact: On the same day, the court in a separate 5-4 ruling (Trump v. Cook) rejected Trump's bid to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, signaling the Fed retains independence.
key_facts.excerpt: While the high court allowed Trump to fire Slaughter, it rejected his bid to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve for the moment. ... In a 5-4 ruling Monday, the Supreme Court rejected the attempt by Trump.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rules police need a warrant for cellphone 'geofence' location data

key_facts.fact: In a 6-3 ruling on June 29 (Chatrie v. United States), the Supreme Court held that law enforcement accessing cellphone location-history data via a geofence warrant is a Fourth Amendment 'search.'
key_facts.excerpt: In the 6-3 ruling, the U.S. top court said that 'an individual has a reasonable expectation of privacy in his cell-phone location information.'

key_facts.fact: Justice Elena Kagan wrote the majority opinion, describing location data as 'a personal journal of a user's movements' that should be shielded from government view.
key_facts.excerpt: Kagan concluded that location data -- which she described as "a personal journal of a user's movements" -- resembles other kinds of private materials such as emails, photographs or documents.

key_facts.fact: The ruling requires authorities to obtain a narrowly tailored warrant showing probable cause before demanding location data from companies such as Google.
key_facts.excerpt: The justices in a 6-3 decision on Monday said that law enforcement accessing such location history data represents a Fourth Amendment search and requires a warrant.

key_facts.fact: The case stemmed from a 2019 Virginia bank robbery, where a geofence warrant captured location data for every cellphone within a roughly 150-300 meter radius; the court remanded to the Fourth Circuit whether that specific warrant was valid.
key_facts.excerpt: The landmark decision stemmed from a case involving a 2019 bank robbery in Virginia. Law enforcement was able to track down the robber using a geofence warrant that included the location data for every cellphone within a 150-meter radius of the robbery.

stories.headline: Genmab's epcoritamab combo cuts DLBCL progression risk 60% in Phase 3 trial

key_facts.fact: Genmab announced June 29 that its Phase 3 EPCORE DLBCL-4 trial of epcoritamab plus lenalidomide met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival in relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
key_facts.excerpt: the trial met its primary objective, demonstrating statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS).

key_facts.fact: The combination reduced the risk of disease progression and death by 60% (HR 0.40) and 56% (HR 0.44) under different US and ex-US censoring rules, with p-values below 0.0001.
key_facts.excerpt: The risk of disease progression and death was reduced by 60% (HR 0.40 [95% CI 0.30, 0.55]; p value < 0.0001) and 56% (HR 0.44 [95% CI 0.33, 0.60]; p value < 0.0001).

key_facts.fact: The chemotherapy-free regimen was compared against standard-of-care rituximab plus gemcitabine plus oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) in adults who had received at least one prior line of treatment.
key_facts.excerpt: EPCORE DLBCL-4 demonstrated improved PFS with a chemotherapy-free combination treatment regimen in patients with R/R DLBCL... compared to standard-of-care, rituximab plus gemcitabine plus oxaliplatin (R-GemOx).

key_facts.fact: Epcoritamab is a subcutaneously administered T-cell engaging bispecific antibody co-developed by Genmab and AbbVie; the safety profile was consistent with the individual agents.
key_facts.excerpt: epcoritamab, a T-cell engaging bispecific antibody administered subcutaneously... The safety profile of epcoritamab when administered in combination with lenalidomide was consistent with the previously reported safety profiles of the individual agents.

stories.headline: Abivax reports positive Phase 3 maintenance results for obefazimod in ulcerative colitis

key_facts.fact: Abivax announced June 29 positive ABTECT Maintenance Part 2 results for obefazimod, showing meaningful clinical benefit in refractory ulcerative colitis patients who were induction non-responders.
key_facts.excerpt: Abivax Reports Positive ABTECT Maintenance Part 2 Results for Obefazimod, Demonstrating Meaningful Clinical Benefit in Refractory UC Patients.

key_facts.fact: The results showed robust efficacy in both induction responders (Part 1) and induction non-responders (Part 2), with safety consistent with the broader obefazimod program and no new safety pattern.
key_facts.excerpt: The robust efficacy results observed in both induction responders (Part 1) and induction non-responders (Part 2) demonstrate a consistent treatment effect... No new safety pattern emerged with the additional cumulative exposure provided by Part 2.

key_facts.fact: The data expand the integrated dataset supporting Abivax's planned New Drug Application for obefazimod in ulcerative colitis, which the company remains on track to submit to the FDA in Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The ABTECT Maintenance Part 2 results expand the integrated clinical dataset supporting the planned New Drug Application ('NDA') for obefazimod in UC. The Company remains on track to submit its NDA to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in the fourth quarter of 2026.
